actual.population: Proposed senior employer-side payroll decision-makers with UK-relevant responsibilities; outsourced payroll users eligible.

records.title: Role in decisions
records.wording: What is your role in decisions about payroll technology, providers or major process changes?
records.purpose: Establish actual decision involvement.
optional_probes: Distinguish recommending, evaluating, implementing and approving.

records.title: Operating context
records.wording: How is payroll currently delivered in your area of responsibility?
records.purpose: Interpret the experience in its operating context.
optional_probes: In-house, outsourced or mixed; broad organisational scale; relevant countries and team responsibilities. Do not request employee records.
For outsourced or mixed delivery, clarify work retained by the employer, information supplied to providers and responsibility for handoffs.

records.title: Improvement priority
records.wording: What, if anything, would you most like to improve about payroll in your organisation?
records.purpose: Identify the participant’s own priority before thematic prompts.
optional_probes: What consequence makes this important, and who is affected?
What currently works well and should be preserved?
Clarify whether the account is first-hand, based on internal reporting, or an interpretation.

records.title: Unmet needs
records.wording: Where, if anywhere, do the payroll technology or services you use or have recently evaluated fall short of your needs?
records.purpose: Identify a concrete capability or service gap without presuming dissatisfaction.
optional_probes: Ask for a specific example, workaround and where the problem begins.
Do you know of an option that would meet this need? If so, what explains why it is not being used?

Use the answer to distinguish perceived availability, suitability, affordability/value, readiness or ownership. Preserve not evaluated, not known and no significant shortfall; do not infer market absence.

records.title: Future priorities
records.wording: Which payroll improvements, if any, do you expect your organisation to prioritise over the next 12–24 months?
records.purpose: Separate ambition from organisational commitment.
optional_probes: For up to two priorities, establish whether each is an idea, under evaluation, in a plan, approved or being delivered. Clarify funding separately where relevant; preserve not known.
What would have to change for this priority to move forward or become less important?

Only after the unaided answer, use AI, automation, integration or outsourcing as optional prompts. Label prompted themes separately. If technology arises, clarify the task, pilot/live stage and oversight rather than assume a common definition.

records.title: Recent decision
records.wording: Thinking about the past 24 months, what is the most recent payroll investment, provider renewal or proposed change in which you had direct involvement?
records.purpose: Anchor the investigation in one recent real case.
optional_probes: Approximate timing, proposal type and direct involvement. Investment may include people, capability, training or controls as well as software and providers.

A substantive approval, renewal, re-scope or go-live decision in an older programme can qualify within the window. Record programme start and selected milestone dates separately; routine activity is not automatically a new decision.

If no recent case is recalled, and the participant is willing, ask: Has an improvement you mentioned been put forward internally? Choose the relevant follow-up: What happened next? Or: What has prevented it being raised?

Only never-raised needs are pre-proposal. If a qualifying recent case emerges, confirm it and resume Q007–Q013. Older-only or uncertain cases stay separately labelled context; otherwise continue to Q014. Do not repeat a declined request to share a case.

records.title: Decision reached
records.wording: What decision had been reached on that proposal as of today?
records.purpose: Establish the actual decision position independently of delivery.
optional_probes: Approved, declined, deferred, withdrawn/abandoned, pending, no formal approval required, not known or prefer not to disclose.
Separately ask what has been implemented, if applicable. Preserve chronology where an earlier approval was subsequently changed.

records.title: Original trigger
records.wording: What prompted this proposal or review?
records.purpose: Connect the case with its initial need, intended outcome and opportunity.
optional_probes: What improvement was the proposal meant to deliver, and how would you know it had worked?
After the open answer, clarify any mandatory deadline, lifecycle/contract timing or discretionary opportunity. Do not presume failure or force a single trigger.

records.title: Authority and influence
records.wording: Who had the authority to approve or stop the proposal?
records.purpose: Identify decision power and conditions.
optional_probes: Sponsor, budget owner, final sign-off and veto or condition-setting roles.
Record functions rather than names. Separate known facts from the participant’s understanding.

records.title: Evidence requested
records.wording: What evidence, if any, was requested to assess the proposal?
records.purpose: Establish the business-case requirements and what value meant in this case.
optional_probes: After the unaided answer, select relevant probes: baseline/measure, cost scope, who expected to benefit, risk, compliance, continuity, capacity, references or a pilot.

Clarify implementation, ongoing support, training and transition costs if they mattered. Distinguish reduced spending from capacity at unchanged spending; do not monetise every benefit or double count.
Do not request confidential documents or exact budgets; not measured or not known are valid answers.

records.title: Evidence that mattered
records.wording: Which evidence, if any, appeared to influence the decision most?
records.purpose: Distinguish evidence produced from evidence believed to affect a decision.
optional_probes: What makes you say it mattered?
Did the proposal or decision change after the evidence was supplied?

For a pending proposal ask: Which evidence, if any, has appeared to influence the assessment so far? For deferred cases retain the main question. For both pending and deferred cases also ask: What evidence, if any, is still needed before a decision can be made? Record routed wording.

routed_wording.pending: Which evidence, if any, has appeared to influence the assessment so far?
routed_wording.pending_or_deferred_follow_up: What evidence, if any, is still needed before a decision can be made?
routed_wording.deferred: Retain the main question to capture evidence behind the deferral, then ask the follow-up.

records.title: Alternatives and choice
records.wording: What other options were considered?
records.purpose: Understand the choice set and selected option.
optional_probes: Renewal, keeping the present arrangement, process change, another provider/platform, mixed solution or no change.
Which option, if any, was selected, and why? Retaining an incumbent is an option, not a decision disposition.
Where relevant, clarify whether staying was preferred on merit, constrained by transition or contract timing, or both. Do not assume lock-in.

records.title: Conditions and constraints
records.wording: What conditions or concerns, if any, most affected whether or when the proposal could proceed?
records.purpose: Explain conditions enabling progress, observed results and constraints.
optional_probes: After the unaided answer, select relevant probes: affordability, migration, integration, upstream data ownership, continuity, compliance, security, skills, training, adoption, capacity or competing priorities.
Ask what enabled progress as well as what constrained it. If useful, ask what supplier action could have reduced the barrier; label that as a proposed remedy rather than an observed effect.

If delivery permits: What has actually changed, and how is the result being assessed? Clarify the benefit owner, baseline/measure and assessment date where known. Where time or capacity was released, ask where it went.

Keep expected benefit, go-live, observed change and attribution separate. Not measured, not yet assessed, not applicable, not known and prefer not to disclose are distinct; none automatically means failure.

records.title: Next research question
records.wording: What is one question about payroll investment that you think the profession should answer next?
records.purpose: Retain priorities beyond the researcher’s assumptions and inform future research.
optional_probes: Optional: advice to another payroll leader facing a comparable decision.
Answering does not imply council membership, recontact or attribution permission.

routing.no_recent_case: Ask Q001–Q006. If willing, clarify whether a need was raised. Never-raised needs are pre-proposal; older-only or uncertain cases remain contextual. If no eligible recent case emerges, continue to Q014 and exclude from the recent-decision-case base.
routing.recent_case: Ask all core questions for a confirmed recent case or substantive recent decision milestone. Select relevant probes; record programme start and selected decision dates separately.
routing.recalled_recent_case: If the no-case follow-up reveals an eligible recent case, confirm timing and direct involvement then resume Q007–Q013.
routing.case_not_shared: Respect a decision not to share. Do not use the follow-up to repeat a declined request; continue to Q014.
routing.written_mode: Same core wording and routing, selective follow-ups, distinguish written responses.

priority_probes: No-case clarification where relevant and welcome
Intended outcome and baseline/measure where known
Observed result and benefit assessment where delivery permits
analysis_rules: Separate future priorities from selected historical case.
Code decision disposition, chosen option and implementation status separately.
Code benefit assessment separately from delivery: measured or observed change is not implied by go-live.
Never-raised needs, older context and confirmed recent cases use different bases; do not force uncertainty into a case category.
Gap explanations are participant-attributed, may overlap and do not prove that a market capability is absent.
Record unanswered, not asked, not applicable, not known and prefer not to disclose separately.
Keep quotations separate from paraphrase; participant attribution does not prove causation.
No automatic population percentages or saturation claim from 6–10 contributions.

critical_anti_anchoring: CFO language is already in S01-D/S05-D/S10-D; S05-D and S10-D already presuppose permanent-leader recruitment. Repetition of these premises in answers cannot establish actual market authority or required solution.
scope_limit: Verifies fidelity and boundaries of the bridge, not historical external facts, actual employer behaviour, recruitment capability or an empirical payroll authority map.
